minutes.headline: Personnel Committee voted through several SAP edits and asked for a 10-grade, 8-step salary grid option next meeting.
minutes.summary: The committee worked through the revised Salary Administration Plan (SAP) section by section, voting on changes to hours of work, step increases, hiring rate, grievance procedure and paid holidays. It left the layoff/seniority language as originally written and set aside the discipline section for later. It then began reviewing the salary survey and grid, and scheduled a Monday meeting to prepare warrant articles for town meeting.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment at the start; none is evident in the captions.
A speaker (Casey) asked whether the inflation rate would be considered when setting the cost-of-living adjustments for the next three years.
A department head (Barb) said many department heads are at the top of their grades and receive only the cost-of-living increase, and asked for that to be considered.

budget_items.what_was_said: Julie presented pay-range data from comparison communities against Lunenburg's FY22 ranges, showing Lunenburg lower at the starting steps.
Members discussed starting grade 1 step 1 at the state minimum wage, which would make every grade more competitive.
The current grid has percentage increases between steps and between grades; members also discussed reducing the number of grades and steps.
A member cited the town manager's February presentation on the impact of a cola for non-union employees through FY27, and clarified that the cola is paid on top of step increases.
A speaker asked whether inflation would be considered; the chair noted the federal government set a similar COLA and that bargaining units are locked into theirs.

decisions.decision: Section 9 layoffs: the committee agreed by consensus to leave the original seniority language as it was, reverting to the version from three sessions earlier.
Section 27 discipline: set aside to the next meeting; Julie to check with Heather whether the steps missing from the charter should be reinstated.
Section 20 personal leave hours-to-days change treated as an edit already voted, so no new vote was taken.
Julie to present salary grid options at the next meeting, including a 10-grade, 8-step version and how employees would be placed.
Next meeting set for Monday March 14 at five o'clock, before caucus.
Three warrant articles planned: SAP bylaw changes, new positions added to the salary plan, and the salary grids.

what_happened.line: The Personnel Committee voted through changes to the Salary Administration Plan on hiring rate, grievance procedure, paid holidays and step-increase eligibility for reclassified staff.
The committee agreed by consensus to keep the original layoff and seniority language, returning to the version from three sessions earlier.
The discipline section was set aside to the next meeting, pending a check on whether steps missing from the charter should be reinstated.
The committee began reviewing the salary survey, which showed Lunenburg lower at the starting steps, and asked for a 10-grade, 8-step grid option.
Three warrant articles are planned for town meeting: plan bylaw changes, new positions, and the salary grids.

why_it_matters: These edits set how non-union town employees are hired, advanced and paid, and the salary grid and new positions are headed to town meeting, where residents will be asked to vote on them.
The survey comparison and cost-of-living discussion bear on what the town budget, mostly taxes, would carry for non-union pay in future years.
watch_next: Monday March 14 at five o'clock, before caucus: salary grid options, including a 10-grade, 8-step version, and the discipline section.
The three warrant articles (plan bylaw changes, new positions, salary grids) for town meeting.
